notes: A fixed number of moves, guards on set patrols, and one target to reach is a logic puzzle of movement, so Puzzle leads; Strategy is named second because what actually gets built is its board game, and taking its Board & Card Games preset and tile-grid row is only possible with the file loaded. None of Puzzle's own shapes fit — puzzle-open assumes a plaza or garden, rooms-sequence a run of sealed chambers — so I took board-grid from the shared catalogue: the answers describe a literal board-game diorama of a small modern mansion with model-like pieces on a compact 8x8 tile grid, viewed three-quarter, which is a board acted on rather than moved through, hence P0 plus SET. Deciding without a user: the ten-move limit and the guard patrol routes are gameplay laid over that board, and because the grid is uniform and trivially connected its topology needs no procedural guarantee, so I did not add P6 the way puzzle-maze would. The target piece and the patrolling guards match no option in either loaded file, so they ride as free-text set content rather than being forced into npc-population, which is for non-hostile inhabitants.
